transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-05-12 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 36 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Sam Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Zenly Head of ML), Priya Shah (Zenly Eng Lead), Liam O'Connor (Zenly CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG quickstart + free credits, time-to-first-token, and criteria for evaluating hosted vs Dedicated/Private. Customer wants low friction eval path for engineers and clarity on security/compliance for later procurement.

Topics: quickstart, free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated, SOC2/KMS, data residency concerns, quotas/rate-limiting, benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, i run the west AE coverage, with me is Sam our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Jordan: good, thanks. morning. we're excited to hear about the quickstart, trying to get our engs up and running this week.
[00:12] Priya: hi all, quick note, we're evaluating hosted first then dedicated if we see predictable cost/throughput needs. main ask is time-to-first-token and whether devs can prototype without procurement friction.
[00:21] Alex: totally understood. that's exactly the PLG path we built for. Sam, wanna run the quickstart highlights?
[00:25] Sam: sure. so quickstart is basically a five-step flow: sign up, get free credits applied, create an API key, run a couple of sample calls (text generation, embeddings), then optionally install SDK and integrate. typical time-to-first-token we see is under 10 minutes for engineers. caveat: depends on CORS, internal firewall, key rotation.
[00:42] Liam: under ten minutes huh, thats ideal. what's in the free credits, like limits?
[00:46] Alex: good question. credits cover runway for prototyping — typically enough for a few thousand tokens of generation plus some embeddings. we'll share the exact redemption doc but it's straightforward: redeem, associated account gets credit, single-use per company.
[00:58] Jordan: do you require SSO to sign up? our security team will flag self-serve accounts without SSO.
[01:03] Sam: not required for initial quickstart; you can sign up with email. for enterprise we support SSO/SAML and enforced SSO at signup for dedicated/private. we can also create a sandbox account that ties into your SSO if needed.
[01:16] Priya: what's the difference in latency and cost between hosted and dedicated for 2k token responses? we care a lot about 1-2s latencies for short responses.
[01:25] Sam: so hosted is multi-tenant with optimized routing; for typical open models we often hit 200-500ms for short prompts, but for long 2k token generations it depends — you'll see higher tail latencies. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity so tails are tighter and throughput predictable, but costs more. i'll follow up with a simple bench matrix.
[01:41] Jordan: can you run a sample with our prompt set? we can anonymize it.
[01:44] Alex: yes please, that's actually one of the recommended pilots — send a small prompt corpus and we'll run a benchmark on hosted and a dedicated profile to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[01:52] Liam: related, what about data retention and logs - will user prompts stay in Redwood? we have compliance constraints.
[01:59] Sam: hosted has configurable retention; by default we do not use customer data for training, and you can set retention to short windows or disable persistent logging for sensitive routes. Dedicated/Private options give you more control — in Private deployments data can remain in your VPC and not cross Redwood control plane depending on the package. we'll send the SOC2 and security packet detailing KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[02:19] Priya: KMS integration—can we bring our own key?
[02:22] Sam: yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports customer-managed keys in select regions, i'll mark that in the security doc.
[02:29] Jordan: any gotchas on onboarding for engs? SDK languages?
[02:33] Alex: SDKs in python, node, go — examples in our quickstart repo. typical friction points are firewall egress, internal proxies, and CORS for in-browser calls — we advise using a backend token exchange.
[02:45] Priya: ok that tracks. what's the quota model? rate limits?
[02:49] Sam: self-serve accounts have conservative rate limits to protect stability; you can request limit increases from within the console. Dedicated comes with committed throughput and SLA. we'll include example quotas and steps to raise them in the docs.
[03:00] Jordan: would you recommend starting on hosted for prototyping then moving to dedicated for pilot?
[03:03] Alex: yes that's the common flow: hosted to validate product/quality, then reserved capacity when you need predictable monthly cost and latency SLAs. if you're in regulated space start the security conversation early.
[03:12] Liam: procurement wise, how fast can we go from POC to committed dedicated?
[03:16] Sam: depends on capacity and contract, but usually 2-6 weeks once terms are agreed. for Private on-prem it's longer due to infra setup.
[03:24] Jordan: what about model catalog — are you hosting foundation models or do we bring our own?
[03:28] Alex: we provide a curated model catalog (open models we benchmark) and support custom model uploads for dedicated/private deployments. we also have quantized profiles to cut cost.
[03:36] Priya: any references or benchmark sheets we can look at?
[03:38] Alex: yes, i will share a benchmark spreadsheet and the quickstart repo link.
[03:42] (short crosstalk)
[03:45] Jordan: any security checklist we can hand to procurement?
[03:48] Sam: we'll share our security packet — SOC2, ISO excerpts, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS notes, audit logs, and sample contract clauses.
[03:56] Alex: ok to recap next steps — i'll send quickstart guide + free credits instructions and the security packet; sam will prepare a small benchmark for hosted vs dedicated on a 2k token workload; jordan will share an anonymized prompt set and expected QPS. schedule a follow up to review results next week?
[04:14] Jordan: works for us, thanks.
[04:17] Priya: one more thing — can you give a ballpark cost per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated?
[04:21] Sam: ballpark varies by model; hosted is typically cheaper for low volume but rises with usage; dedicated reduces unit cost at committed volume. i'll include a sample cost model in the follow-up.
[04:32] Liam: great, thanks everyone.
[04:34] Alex: thanks all — we'll send docs and follow up on the benchmarks.

Action items (recorded):
- Alex Moreno to send quickstart guide, free credits redemption doc, and quickstart repo link.
